title: Bing AI citations: homepages were 6.8% of 883,000
why: Expected: the homepage carries most AI citations for a site. Found: in a 26-brand Bing sample, homepages were 6.8% of citations and guides, product and support pages made up most of the rest.
source_check: Read 24 Nov 2026 via the article. Study: 26 brands, 9 verticals, over 1.1M citations in the overview export, 883,000+ on 10,861 URLs, from Bing AI Performance Reporting (public preview since February 2026), spring and fall pulls. Author notes backfilling, machine-initiated queries counted, and pooled figures lean toward large sites. Single vendor tool.

thread: Why it matters: a homepage audit checks the page a buyer sees first. The citation mix points to guides, product pages and support articles instead.
Monday morning: pull your most-cited URLs from AI reporting, if you have it. Check title, description and schema on each. Fix the most-cited ones first.
Limits: one vendor's data, 26 brands, larger sites weighted in. Source: Search Engine Journal analysis of Bing AI Performance pulls. Confidence: medium.

drafts.text:
Bing's AI reporting says something uncomfortable for homepage-first audits.

A Search Engine Journal analysis pulled Bing AI citation data for 26 brands: more than 883,000 citations on 10,861 URLs, spring and fall 2026. Homepages were 6.8% of citations. Editorial guides were 18.3%. Product pages were 16.7%. Support and how-to pages were 11.2%. PDFs were over 6%.

Monday morning: take the ten URLs your brand is cited on most, if your reporting shows them, and check each for a title, a description and the schema it needs.

Method note: one vendor's data, 26 brands, large sites weighted in, read through a secondary write-up. Confidence: medium. Not a sample of the web.
